name: Pioneer 11
first: First spacecraft to fly past Saturn (1979-09-01); demonstrated the gravity-assist that sent Voyager 2 onward
description: Twin of Pioneer 10, launched a year later. Pioneer 11 used Jupiter’s gravity to bend its trajectory toward Saturn — the canonical proof of gravity-assist propulsion, the technique that later enabled the Voyager Grand Tour. At Saturn it discovered the F ring and the moon Epimetheus. Carries the same Pioneer plaque as its twin. Signal lost 1995-09-30 from a heliocentric distance of ~43 AU; the spacecraft is now heading toward the constellation Aquila.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Atlas-Centaur from Cape Canaveral on a Jupiter-Saturn gravity-assist trajectory.

events.label: JUPITER FLYBY
events.note: Used Jupiter assist to bend onto a Saturn-bound path.

events.label: SATURN CLOSEST APPROACH
events.note: First images of the planet at close range; discovered the F ring and Epimetheus.
